request.system:
You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

VERIFICATION TRIAGE INVARIANT (mandatory)
When verification capacity is limited, prioritize inherited beliefs that are both highly consequential to the current decision and insufficiently supported for the objective being optimized.
request.user:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation. Fewer required fields at
    signup produced a durable lift.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; a
    demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB
    segments — strong acquisition and revenue lift.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers and added
    qualified revenue without hurting retention.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shorter onboarding improved time-to-value and completion rates.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging improved week-one engagement.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

first.rationale: Two candidates dominate this week's slot: promotional_pricing (the direct answer to the competitor's entry pricing) and simplify_onboarding (the direct answer to the -4% completion / -6% activation decay). Verification budget therefore goes to the beliefs that are most consequential AND least supported for the stated objective of sustainable long-term QUALIFIED revenue. memory_73 is first priority: it is the only memory that would justify a discount response, and as recorded it reports 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' with no statement about retention, expansion, or account quality — exactly the failure mode where a promo wins the quarter and imports churn-prone, price-anchored accounts. If the archived record turns out to measure only first-order acquisition/booked revenue over a short window, that memory cannot carry a competitive-response decision. memory_86 is second priority: it is the load-bearing evidence for my intended action, but its recorded outcome is time-to-value and completion rate — funnel metrics, not qualified revenue. memory_31 partially backstops it ('durable lift' in SMB activation), which is why memory_31 is not the one I spend the pull on. memory_44 and memory_57 are not verified because enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive do not address either observed regression and are not this week's decision. I currently intend simplify_onboarding at standard scale: it attacks the two measured declines at their shared upstream point, its evidence base (memory_31 + memory_86) is corroborated across two independent consolidations, and unlike a discount it cannot degrade revenue quality by construction. The honest gap I am carrying is that neither onboarding memory demonstrates a downstream qualified-revenue effect, so I will instrument the test on activation-to-qualified-conversion, not completion rate alone, and treat a completion lift with flat downstream conversion as a null result rather than a win. If memory_73's archived record shows durable retention alongside the revenue lift, promotional_pricing becomes the stronger competitive answer and I would switch to it as a small guarded test with explicit stop conditions on cohort retention and discount-cohort expansion.

final.rationale: The archive resolved the decision cleanly. exp_73 confirms the failure mode I flagged: the +18% qualified revenue was real but came with -12% 30-day retention, and the original record explicitly instructs against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. Memory_73 as consolidated had silently dropped that caveat, so the discount response to the competitor is off the table under a sustainable long-term qualified-revenue objective — matching the competitor on price would buy signups that do not survive the first renewal cycle, and would do so precisely into the price-sensitive segment already churning. exp_86 came back stronger than the consolidated version: not just completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days but 30-day retention +3%, which is the downstream signal I said was missing. Combined with memory_31's independent finding of durable SMB activation lift from fewer signup fields, simplify_onboarding is now the best-evidenced action available and it targets the two actually-measured regressions (-4% completion, -6% activation) at their shared upstream point. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout: the retention evidence is 30-day, not renewal-cycle, so I still do not have direct proof that an onboarding lift propagates to qualified revenue at horizon — exp_86's conclusion is 'confirmed' for funnel and short-window retention only. I therefore keep the primary readout as activation-to-qualified-conversion with a stop condition if completion rises while downstream conversion or 30-day retention goes flat-to-negative, which would indicate I am admitting under-qualified accounts through a lower-friction door. I am also not treating this as a competitive response: it does not address the price-sensitive accounts the competitor is taking, and that gap remains open and unaddressed this week. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is the reasonable second choice but is single-sourced and unverified; enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive address neither observed decline.
